transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi Dr. Smith. Well, the main reason I’m here is that I'm having a lot of trouble at work. I'm a nurse, and on the floor, I just lose my train of thought constantly. It's getting really difficult to manage. Like, an IV pump will beep, or I'll hear someone ask another nurse a question, or a call light goes off, and... suddenly I’ve just completely forgotten what patient flow issue I was working on. It just happens all the time.
Have you struggled with this kind of distractibility and forgetfulness since you were a child, or is this a relatively new problem for you?

No, it's definitely not a new problem. It's been like this since I was a kid, honestly. Even back in elementary school, my teachers would write on my report cards that I was bright but careless. I was always losing my worksheets or just... forgetting to turn in my homework altogether. My mom actually had to sit down with me every single night just to make sure I got it done and stayed on track.
